To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the conditions under which GR2 forms a complex and crystallizes in CHAPS detergent.

we have developed an improved purification protocol for GRK2 that yields a highly purified protein preparation that can be crystallized in the presence of Gbeta1gamma2 and that we have obtained a high-resolution diffraction data set from crystals of the complex.

we have developed an improved purification scheme for the G protein-coupling receptor kinase 2, determined conditions under which GRk2 forms a complex with Gbeta(1)-gamma(2) and crystallized the complex in CHAPS detergent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the desensitization of G protein-couled receptors (GPCRs).
the molecular mechanisms underlying the desensitization of G protein-couled receptors (GPCRs) by G protein-coupling receptor kinases (GRKs).
the molecular basis of signal termination by G protein-coupling receptor kinases, and the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystallographic studies have not yet been completed.
the GRK2-PH domain has been crystallized for the first time in complex with a Gbeta(1)-gamma(2) subunit, and that a high-resolution structure of the complex is likely to be obtained.
the crystal structure of GRK2-Gbeta(1) gamma(2) complex will provide a structural basis for the molecular understanding of the regulation of the GPCR signaling pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallization conditions for GRK2 have been improved and that the first crystals of the GRK-Gbetagamma(2) complex have been obtained.
the GRK2-PH domain is a Gbeta(1)-selective binding protein.

we have developed a purification scheme for GRKR2, determined the crystallization conditions for a complex between GRK2 and Gbetagamma, collected diffraction data to 3.0 A resolution and are now in the process of solving the structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to purify and crystallize a complex between GRK2 and the G protein subunits.
the use of the detergent CHAPS in conjunction with a modified purification scheme allows us to purify GRK2 to a high degree of purity and to form complexes with Gbetagamma.
the complex between GRK2 and Gbetagamma has been purified to homogeneity in milligram quantities, which should facilitate structural studies of the complex.
